title: How Language Shapes the Way We Think | Lera Boroditsky | TED

blocks.en_text: So, I'll be speaking to you using language ...
blocks.zh_text: 所以，我将用语言来跟你们交流……

blocks.en_text: because I can.
blocks.zh_text: 因为我会说话。

blocks.en_text: This is one these magical abilities that we humans have.
blocks.zh_text: 这是我们人类拥有的一种神奇能力。

blocks.en_text: We can transmit really complicated thoughts to one another.
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以把非常复杂的想法传递给彼此。

blocks.en_text: So what I'm doing right now is, I'm making sounds with my mouth
blocks.zh_text: 所以我现在在做的事情，就是用嘴巴发出声音

blocks.en_text: as I'm exhaling.
blocks.zh_text: 一边呼气一边发声。

blocks.en_text: I'm making tones and hisses and puffs,
blocks.zh_text: 我在发出各种音调、嘶嘶声和喷气声，

blocks.en_text: and those are creating air vibrations in the air.
blocks.zh_text: 这些声音在空气中产生了振动。

blocks.en_text: Those air vibrations are traveling to you,
blocks.zh_text: 这些空气振动传到你那里，

blocks.en_text: they're hitting your eardrums,
blocks.zh_text: 它们敲击着你的耳膜，

blocks.en_text: and then your brain takes those vibrations from your eardrums
blocks.zh_text: 然后你的大脑把耳膜传来的这些振动

blocks.en_text: and transforms them into thoughts.
blocks.zh_text: 转化成思想。

blocks.en_text: I hope.
blocks.zh_text: 希望如此。

blocks.en_text: I hope that's happening.
blocks.zh_text: 希望这真的在发生。

blocks.en_text: So because of this ability, we humans are able to transmit our ideas
blocks.zh_text: 正因为有这种能力，我们人类才能把想法传递出去

blocks.en_text: across vast reaches of space and time.
blocks.zh_text: 跨越广阔的空间和时间。

blocks.en_text: We're able to transmit knowledge across minds.
blocks.zh_text: 我们能够把知识从一个头脑传到另一个头脑。

blocks.en_text: I can put a bizarre new idea in your mind right now.
blocks.zh_text: 我现在就能把一个稀奇古怪的新想法放进你脑子里。

blocks.en_text: I could say,
blocks.zh_text: 我可以说，

blocks.en_text: "Imagine a jellyfish waltzing in a library
blocks.zh_text: “想象一只水母在图书馆里跳华尔兹，

blocks.en_text: while thinking about quantum mechanics."
blocks.zh_text: 一边还想着量子力学。”

blocks.en_text: Now, if everything has gone relatively well in your life so far,
blocks.zh_text: 如果你到目前为止的人生还算比较正常，

blocks.en_text: you probably haven't had that thought before.
blocks.zh_text: 你以前大概没想过这个画面。

blocks.en_text: But now I've just made you think it,
blocks.zh_text: 但现在我刚刚让你想到了它，

blocks.en_text: through language.
blocks.zh_text: 通过语言。

blocks.en_text: Now of course, there isn't just one language in the world,
blocks.zh_text: 当然，世界上不只有一种语言，

blocks.en_text: there are about 7,000 languages spoken around the world.
blocks.zh_text: 全世界大约有七千种语言在使用。

blocks.en_text: And all the languages differ from one another in all kinds of ways.
blocks.zh_text: 而所有语言在方方面面都彼此不同。

blocks.en_text: Some languages have different sounds,
blocks.zh_text: 有些语言发音不同，

blocks.en_text: they have different vocabularies,
blocks.zh_text: 词汇不同，

blocks.en_text: and they also have different structures --
blocks.zh_text: 结构也不同——

blocks.en_text: very importantly, different structures.
blocks.zh_text: 非常重要的是，结构不同。

blocks.en_text: That begs the question:
blocks.zh_text: 这就引出了一个问题：

blocks.en_text: Does the language we speak shape the way we think?
blocks.zh_text: 我们所说的语言会塑造我们的思维方式吗？

blocks.en_text: Now, this is an ancient question.
blocks.zh_text: 这是一个古老的问题。

blocks.en_text: People have been speculating about this question forever.
blocks.zh_text: 人们一直在思考这个问题。

blocks.en_text: Charlemagne, Holy Roman emperor, said,
blocks.zh_text: 神圣罗马帝国皇帝查理曼说过，

blocks.en_text: "To have a second language is to have a second soul" --
blocks.zh_text: “掌握第二种语言，就是拥有第二个灵魂”——

blocks.en_text: strong statement that language crafts reality.
blocks.zh_text: 这是个强有力的说法，认为语言塑造了现实。

blocks.en_text: But on the other hand, Shakespeare has Juliet say,
blocks.zh_text: 但另一方面，莎士比亚让朱丽叶说，

blocks.en_text: "What's in a name?
blocks.zh_text: “名字算什么？

blocks.en_text: A rose by any other name would smell as sweet."
blocks.zh_text: 玫瑰换个名字，照样芬芳。”

blocks.en_text: Well, that suggests that maybe language doesn't craft reality.
blocks.zh_text: 这似乎说明，语言也许并不塑造现实。

blocks.en_text: These arguments have gone back and forth for thousands of years.
blocks.zh_text: 这些争论已经来回持续了几千年。

blocks.en_text: But until recently, there hasn't been any data
blocks.zh_text: 但直到最近，都还没有任何数据

blocks.en_text: to help us decide either way.
blocks.zh_text: 能帮我们做出判断。

blocks.en_text: Recently, in my lab and other labs around the world,
blocks.zh_text: 最近，在我的实验室和世界各地其他实验室里，

blocks.en_text: we've started doing research,
blocks.zh_text: 我们开始做研究，

blocks.en_text: and now we have actual scientific data to weigh in on this question.
blocks.zh_text: 现在我们有真正的科学数据来探讨这个问题了。

blocks.en_text: So let me tell you about some of my favorite examples.
blocks.zh_text: 那么，让我给你们讲几个我最喜欢的例子。

blocks.en_text: I'll start with an example from an Aboriginal community in Australia
blocks.zh_text: 我先举一个澳大利亚原住民社区的例子

blocks.en_text: that I had the chance to work with.
blocks.zh_text: 我曾有机会和他们合作。

blocks.en_text: These are the Kuuk Thaayorre people.
blocks.zh_text: 他们就是库克萨约尔人。

blocks.en_text: They live in Pormpuraaw at the very west edge of Cape York.
blocks.zh_text: 他们住在约克角最西边的波姆普拉瓦。

blocks.en_text: What's cool about Kuuk Thaayorre is,
blocks.zh_text: 库克萨约尔语有意思的地方在于，

blocks.en_text: in Kuuk Thaayorre, they don't use words like "left" and "right,"
blocks.zh_text: 在库克萨约尔语里，他们不用“左”和“右”这样的词，

blocks.en_text: and instead, everything is in cardinal directions:
blocks.zh_text: 而是所有东西都用基本方位来表示：

blocks.en_text: north, south, east and west.
blocks.zh_text: 北、南、东、西。

blocks.en_text: And when I say everything, I really mean everything.
blocks.zh_text: 我说所有东西，真的是指所有东西。

blocks.en_text: You would say something like,
blocks.zh_text: 你会说这样的话，

blocks.en_text: "Oh, there's an ant on your southwest leg."
blocks.zh_text: “哦，你西南方向的腿上有一只蚂蚁。”

blocks.en_text: Or, "Move your cup to the north-northeast a little bit."
blocks.zh_text: 或者，“把你的杯子往北偏东北挪一点。”

blocks.en_text: In fact, the way that you say "hello" in Kuuk Thaayorre is you say,
blocks.zh_text: 其实，在库克萨约尔语里，你说“你好”的方式是说，

blocks.en_text: "Which way are you going?"
blocks.zh_text: “你要往哪边走？”

blocks.en_text: And the answer should be,
blocks.zh_text: 而回答应该是，

blocks.en_text: "North-northeast in the far distance.
blocks.zh_text: “往北偏东北，很远的地方。

blocks.en_text: How about you?"
blocks.zh_text: 你呢？”

blocks.en_text: So imagine as you're walking around your day,
blocks.zh_text: 所以想象一下，你一天里走来走去，

blocks.en_text: every person you greet,
blocks.zh_text: 你问候的每一个人，

blocks.en_text: you have to report your heading direction.
blocks.zh_text: 你都得报告自己的行进方向。

blocks.en_text: But that would actually get you oriented pretty fast, right?
blocks.zh_text: 但这其实会让你很快就能辨清方向，对吧？

blocks.en_text: Because you literally couldn't get past "hello,"
blocks.zh_text: 因为你要是不知道自己在往哪边走，

blocks.en_text: if you didn't know which way you were going.
blocks.zh_text: 就根本连“你好”这一关都过不去。

blocks.en_text: In fact, people who speak languages like this stay oriented really well.
blocks.zh_text: 事实上，说这类语言的人方向感特别好。

blocks.en_text: They stay oriented better than we used to think humans could.
blocks.zh_text: 他们的方向感比我们过去以为人类能做到的还要好。

blocks.en_text: We used to think that humans were worse than other creatures
blocks.zh_text: 我们过去以为人类比其他生物差

blocks.en_text: because of some biological excuse:
blocks.zh_text: 还找了些生物学上的借口：

blocks.en_text: "Oh, we don't have magnets in our beaks or in our scales."
blocks.zh_text: “哦，我们的喙里或者鳞片里没有磁铁嘛。”

blocks.en_text: No; if your language and your culture trains you to do it,
blocks.zh_text: 不对；如果你的语言和文化训练你这么做，

blocks.en_text: actually, you can do it.
blocks.zh_text: 其实你是能做到的。

blocks.en_text: There are humans around the world who stay oriented really well.
blocks.zh_text: 世界上有些人的方向感特别好。

blocks.en_text: And just to get us in agreement
blocks.zh_text: 为了让大家达成共识，

blocks.en_text: about how different this is from the way we do it,
blocks.zh_text: 明白这和我们做事的方式有多不同，

blocks.en_text: I want you all to close your eyes for a second
blocks.zh_text: 我想请大家先闭上眼睛，

blocks.en_text: and point southeast.
blocks.zh_text: 指一下东南方向。

blocks.en_text: Keep your eyes closed. Point.
blocks.zh_text: 闭上眼睛，指。

blocks.en_text: OK, so you can open your eyes.
blocks.zh_text: 好，可以睁开眼睛了。

blocks.en_text: I see you guys pointing there, there, there, there, there ...
blocks.zh_text: 我看到你们指那边、那边、那边、那边、那边……

blocks.en_text: I don't know which way it is myself --
blocks.zh_text: 我自己都不知道东南是哪边——

blocks.en_text: You have not been a lot of help.
blocks.zh_text: 你们也没帮上什么忙。

blocks.en_text: So let's just say the accuracy in this room was not very high.
blocks.zh_text: 所以说，这个房间里的准确率不太高。

blocks.en_text: This is a big difference in cognitive ability across languages, right?
blocks.zh_text: 这是不同语言之间认知能力的巨大差异，对吧？

blocks.en_text: Where one group -- very distinguished group like you guys --
blocks.zh_text: 其中一组——像你们这样非常出色的一组——

blocks.en_text: doesn't know which way is which,
blocks.zh_text: 不知道哪边是哪边，

blocks.en_text: but in another group,
blocks.zh_text: 但在另一组里，

blocks.en_text: I could ask a five-year-old and they would know.
blocks.zh_text: 我随便问一个五岁小孩，他们都知道。

blocks.en_text: There are also really big differences in how people think about time.
blocks.zh_text: 人们思考时间的方式也有很大的差异。

blocks.en_text: So here I have pictures of my grandfather at different ages.
blocks.zh_text: 这里有几张我祖父不同年龄的照片。

blocks.en_text: And if I ask an English speaker to organize time,
blocks.zh_text: 如果我让一个说英语的人来排列时间，

blocks.en_text: they might lay it out this way,
blocks.zh_text: 他们可能会这样摆，

blocks.en_text: from left to right.
blocks.zh_text: 从左到右。

blocks.en_text: This has to do with writing direction.
blocks.zh_text: 这和书写方向有关。

blocks.en_text: If you were a speaker of Hebrew or Arabic,
blocks.zh_text: 如果你说的是希伯来语或阿拉伯语，

blocks.en_text: you might do it going in the opposite direction,
blocks.zh_text: 你可能会反过来排，

blocks.en_text: from right to left.
blocks.zh_text: 从右到左。

blocks.en_text: But how would the Kuuk Thaayorre,
blocks.zh_text: 但库克萨约雷人——

blocks.en_text: this Aboriginal group I just told you about, do it?
blocks.zh_text: 就是我刚跟你们提到的这个原住民群体——会怎么排呢？

blocks.en_text: They don't use words like "left" and "right."
blocks.zh_text: 他们不用“左”和“右”这样的词。

blocks.en_text: Let me give you hint.
blocks.zh_text: 我给你们个提示。

blocks.en_text: When we sat people facing south,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们让人面朝南坐时，

blocks.en_text: they organized time from left to right.
blocks.zh_text: 他们把时间从左排到右。

blocks.en_text: When we sat them facing north,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们让他们面朝北坐时，

blocks.en_text: they organized time from right to left.
blocks.zh_text: 他们把时间从右排到左。

blocks.en_text: When we sat them facing east,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们让他们面朝东坐时，

blocks.en_text: time came towards the body.
blocks.zh_text: 时间是从前往身体这边来的。

blocks.en_text: What's the pattern?
blocks.zh_text: 规律是什么？

blocks.en_text: East to west, right?
blocks.zh_text: 从东到西，对吧？

blocks.en_text: So for them, time doesn't actually get locked on the body at all,
blocks.zh_text: 所以对他们来说，时间根本不是固定在身体上的，

blocks.en_text: it gets locked on the landscape.
blocks.zh_text: 而是固定在地形上的。

blocks.en_text: So for me, if I'm facing this way,
blocks.zh_text: 所以对我来说，如果我朝这边，

blocks.en_text: then time goes this way,
blocks.zh_text: 那时间就往这边走，

blocks.en_text: and if I'm facing this way, then time goes this way.
blocks.zh_text: 如果我朝这边，那时间就往这边走。

blocks.en_text: I'm facing this way, time goes this way --
blocks.zh_text: 我朝这边，时间就往这边走——

blocks.en_text: very egocentric of me to have the direction of time chase me around
blocks.zh_text: 我真是太以自我为中心了，每次转身都让时间的方向跟着我转。

blocks.en_text: every time I turn my body.
blocks.zh_text: 每次我转动身体的时候。

blocks.en_text: For the Kuuk Thaayorre, time is locked on the landscape.
blocks.zh_text: 对库克萨约雷人来说，时间是固定在地形上的。

blocks.en_text: It's a dramatically different way of thinking about time.
blocks.zh_text: 这是一种截然不同的时间思维方式。

blocks.en_text: Here's another really smart human trick.
blocks.zh_text: 还有一个非常聪明的人类小技巧。

blocks.en_text: Suppose I ask you how many penguins are there.
blocks.zh_text: 假设我问你那儿有多少只企鹅。

blocks.en_text: Well, I bet I know how you'd solve that problem if you solved it.
blocks.zh_text: 我敢打赌，如果你真去数，我知道你会怎么解决这个问题。

blocks.en_text: You went, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight."
blocks.zh_text: 你会说：“一、二、三、四、五、六、七、八。”

blocks.en_text: You counted them.
blocks.zh_text: 你把它们数了一遍。

blocks.en_text: You named each one with a number,
blocks.zh_text: 你给每一只都配上一个数字，

blocks.en_text: and the last number you said was the number of penguins.
blocks.zh_text: 你最后说的那个数字就是企鹅的数量。

blocks.en_text: This is a little trick that you're taught to use as kids.
blocks.zh_text: 这是你小时候被教着用的小技巧。

blocks.en_text: You learn the number list and you learn how to apply it.
blocks.zh_text: 你学会了数字序列，也学会了怎么用它。

blocks.en_text: A little linguistic trick.
blocks.zh_text: 一个小小的语言技巧。

blocks.en_text: Well, some languages don't do this,
blocks.zh_text: 有些语言不这么做，

blocks.en_text: because some languages don't have exact number words.
blocks.zh_text: 因为有些语言没有精确的数字词。

blocks.en_text: They're languages that don't have a word like "seven"
blocks.zh_text: 这些语言里没有像“七”这样的词，

blocks.en_text: or a word like "eight."
blocks.zh_text: 也没有像“八”这样的词。

blocks.en_text: In fact, people who speak these languages don't count,
blocks.zh_text: 事实上，说这些语言的人不数数，

blocks.en_text: and they have trouble keeping track of exact quantities.
blocks.zh_text: 他们也很难记住精确的数量。

blocks.en_text: So, for example, if I ask you to match this number of penguins
blocks.zh_text: 所以，举个例子，如果我让你把这些数量的企鹅

blocks.en_text: to the same number of ducks,
blocks.zh_text: 和同样数量的鸭子配对，

blocks.en_text: you would be able to do that by counting.
blocks.zh_text: 你可以通过数数来做到。

blocks.en_text: But folks who don't have that linguistic trick can't do that.
blocks.zh_text: 但没有这种语言技巧的人就做不到。

blocks.en_text: Languages also differ in how they divide up the color spectrum --
blocks.zh_text: 语言在如何划分色谱方面也有差异——

blocks.en_text: the visual world.
blocks.zh_text: 也就是视觉世界。

blocks.en_text: Some languages have lots of words for colors,
blocks.zh_text: 有些语言有很多表示颜色的词，

blocks.en_text: some have only a couple words, "light" and "dark."
blocks.zh_text: 有些只有几个词，比如“浅色”和“深色”。

blocks.en_text: And languages differ in where they put boundaries between colors.
blocks.zh_text: 而且语言在颜色之间界限的划分上也有差异。

blocks.en_text: So, for example, in English, there's a word for blue
blocks.zh_text: 所以，举个例子，在英语里有一个词表示蓝色

blocks.en_text: that covers all of the colors that you can see on the screen,
blocks.zh_text: 它涵盖了你在屏幕上能看到的所有那些颜色，

blocks.en_text: but in Russian, there isn't a single word.
blocks.zh_text: 但在俄语里，没有单独一个词。

blocks.en_text: Instead, Russian speakers have to differentiate
blocks.zh_text: 相反，说俄语的人必须区分

blocks.en_text: between light blue, "goluboy,"
blocks.zh_text: 浅蓝色“goluboy”

blocks.en_text: and dark blue, "siniy."
blocks.zh_text: 和深蓝色“siniy”。

blocks.en_text: So Russians have this lifetime of experience of, in language,
blocks.zh_text: 所以俄罗斯人一辈子都有这样的经验，在语言上

blocks.en_text: distinguishing these two colors.
blocks.zh_text: 区分这两种颜色。

blocks.en_text: When we test people's ability to perceptually discriminate these colors,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们测试人们在感知上区分这些颜色的能力时，

blocks.en_text: what we find is that Russian speakers are faster
blocks.zh_text: 我们发现说俄语的人反应更快

blocks.en_text: across this linguistic boundary.
blocks.zh_text: 跨越这条语言界限。

blocks.en_text: They're faster to be able to tell the difference
blocks.zh_text: 他们能更快地分辨出区别

blocks.en_text: between a light and dark blue.
blocks.zh_text: 在浅蓝色和深蓝色之间。

blocks.en_text: And when you look at people's brains as they're looking at colors --
blocks.zh_text: 而当你观察人们看颜色时的大脑活动——

blocks.en_text: say you have colors shifting slowly from light to dark blue --
blocks.zh_text: 假设颜色从浅蓝慢慢变到深蓝——

blocks.en_text: the brains of people who use different words for light and dark blue
blocks.zh_text: 那些用不同词表示浅蓝和深蓝的人，他们的大脑

blocks.en_text: will give a surprised reaction as the colors shift from light to dark,
blocks.zh_text: 会在颜色从浅变深时产生惊讶的反应，

blocks.en_text: as if, "Ooh, something has categorically changed,"
blocks.zh_text: 就好像“哦，有什么东西发生了类别上的变化”，

blocks.en_text: whereas the brains of English speakers, for example,
blocks.zh_text: 而比如说，说英语的人的大脑，

blocks.en_text: that don't make this categorical distinction,
blocks.zh_text: 他们不做这种类别区分，

blocks.en_text: don't give that surprise,
blocks.zh_text: 就不会产生那种惊讶，

blocks.en_text: because nothing is categorically changing.
blocks.zh_text: 因为没有任何东西发生类别上的变化。

blocks.en_text: Languages have all kinds of structural quirks.
blocks.zh_text: 语言有各种各样的结构特点。

blocks.en_text: This is one of my favorites.
blocks.zh_text: 这是我最喜欢的一个。

blocks.en_text: Lots of languages have grammatical gender;
blocks.zh_text: 很多语言都有语法性别；

blocks.en_text: every noun gets assigned a gender, often masculine or feminine.
blocks.zh_text: 每个名词都被赋予一个性别，通常是阳性或阴性。

blocks.en_text: And these genders differ across languages.
blocks.zh_text: 而这些性别在不同语言中也不一样。

blocks.en_text: So, for example, the sun is feminine in German but masculine in Spanish,
blocks.zh_text: 所以，举个例子，太阳在德语里是阴性，但在西班牙语里是阳性，

blocks.en_text: and the moon, the reverse.
blocks.zh_text: 而月亮正好相反。

blocks.en_text: Could this actually have any consequence for how people think?
blocks.zh_text: 这真的会对人们的思维方式产生影响吗？

blocks.en_text: Do German speakers think of the sun as somehow more female-like,
blocks.zh_text: 说德语的人会不会觉得太阳在某种程度上更像女性，

blocks.en_text: and the moon somehow more male-like?
blocks.zh_text: 而月亮在某种程度上更像男性？

blocks.en_text: Actually, it turns out that's the case.
blocks.zh_text: 实际上，结果证明确实如此。

blocks.en_text: So if you ask German and Spanish speakers to, say, describe a bridge,
blocks.zh_text: 所以如果你让说德语和说西班牙语的人，比如说，描述一座桥，

blocks.en_text: like the one here --
blocks.zh_text: 就像这里的这座——

blocks.en_text: "bridge" happens to be grammatically feminine in German,
blocks.zh_text: “桥”在德语里恰好是语法阴性，

blocks.en_text: grammatically masculine in Spanish --
blocks.zh_text: 在西班牙语里是语法阳性——

blocks.en_text: German speakers are more likely to say bridges are "beautiful," "elegant"
blocks.zh_text: 说德语的人更可能说桥是“美丽的”“优雅的”

blocks.en_text: and stereotypically feminine words.
blocks.zh_text: 以及那些刻板印象中偏女性化的词。

blocks.en_text: Whereas Spanish speakers will be more likely to say
blocks.zh_text: 而说西班牙语的人则更可能说

blocks.en_text: they're "strong" or "long,"
blocks.zh_text: 桥是“坚固的”或“长的”，

blocks.en_text: these masculine words.
blocks.zh_text: 用的是这些偏男性化的词。

blocks.en_text: Languages also differ in how they describe events, right?
blocks.zh_text: 各种语言在描述事件的方式上也不一样，对吧？

blocks.en_text: You take an event like this, an accident.
blocks.zh_text: 拿这样一个事件来说，一场意外。

blocks.en_text: In English, it's fine to say, "He broke the vase."
blocks.zh_text: 在英语里，说“他打碎了花瓶”是没问题的。

blocks.en_text: In a language like Spanish,
blocks.zh_text: 而在像西班牙语这样的语言里，

blocks.en_text: you might be more likely to say, "The vase broke,"
blocks.zh_text: 你可能更倾向于说“花瓶碎了”，

blocks.en_text: or, "The vase broke itself."
blocks.zh_text: 或者说“花瓶自己碎了”。

blocks.en_text: If it's an accident, you wouldn't say that someone did it.
blocks.zh_text: 如果是意外，你就不会说是某个人干的。

blocks.en_text: In English, quite weirdly, we can even say things like,
blocks.zh_text: 在英语里，挺奇怪的，我们甚至能这样说：

blocks.en_text: "I broke my arm."
blocks.zh_text: “我摔断了我的胳膊。”

blocks.en_text: Now, in lots of languages,
blocks.zh_text: 而在很多语言里，

blocks.en_text: you couldn't use that construction unless you are a lunatic
blocks.zh_text: 你不能用这种说法，除非你是个疯子

blocks.en_text: and you went out looking to break your arm --
blocks.zh_text: 跑出去专门想把自己的胳膊弄断——

blocks.en_text: and you succeeded.
blocks.zh_text: 而且你还真做到了。

blocks.en_text: If it was an accident, you would use a different construction.
blocks.zh_text: 如果是意外，你会用另一种说法。

blocks.en_text: Now, this has consequences.
blocks.zh_text: 这就会带来后果。

blocks.en_text: So, people who speak different languages will pay attention to different things,
blocks.zh_text: 所以，说不同语言的人会关注不同的事情，

blocks.en_text: depending on what their language usually requires them to do.
blocks.zh_text: 取决于他们的语言通常要求他们怎么做。

blocks.en_text: So we show the same accident to English speakers and Spanish speakers,
blocks.zh_text: 我们把同一个意外放给说英语的人和说西班牙语的人看，

blocks.en_text: English speakers will remember who did it,
blocks.zh_text: 说英语的人会记住是谁干的，

blocks.en_text: because English requires you to say, "He did it; he broke the vase."
blocks.zh_text: 因为英语要求你说“是他干的；他打碎了花瓶。”

blocks.en_text: Whereas Spanish speakers might be less likely to remember who did it
blocks.zh_text: 而说西班牙语的人可能不太会记住是谁干的，

blocks.en_text: if it's an accident,
blocks.zh_text: 如果那是个意外的话，

blocks.en_text: but they're more likely to remember that it was an accident.
blocks.zh_text: 但他们更可能记住那是个意外。

blocks.en_text: They're more likely to remember the intention.
blocks.zh_text: 他们更可能记住意图。

blocks.en_text: So, two people watch the same event,
blocks.zh_text: 所以，两个人看同一个事件，

blocks.en_text: witness the same crime,
blocks.zh_text: 目睹同一桩罪行，

blocks.en_text: but end up remembering different things about that event.
blocks.zh_text: 但最终记住的关于那个事件的内容却不一样。

blocks.en_text: This has implications, of course, for eyewitness testimony.
blocks.zh_text: 当然，这对目击者证词是有影响的。

blocks.en_text: It also has implications for blame and punishment.
blocks.zh_text: 这对责任认定和惩罚也有影响。

blocks.en_text: So if you take English speakers
blocks.zh_text: 所以如果你找来说英语的人，

blocks.en_text: and I just show you someone breaking a vase,
blocks.zh_text: 我就给你看有人打碎花瓶的画面，

blocks.en_text: and I say, "He broke the vase," as opposed to "The vase broke,"
blocks.zh_text: 然后我说“他打碎了花瓶”，而不是“花瓶碎了”，

blocks.en_text: even though you can witness it yourself,
blocks.zh_text: 即使你可以亲眼看到，

blocks.en_text: you can watch the video,
blocks.zh_text: 你可以看视频，

blocks.en_text: you can watch the crime against the vase,
blocks.zh_text: 你可以看到对花瓶犯下的这桩“罪行”，

blocks.en_text: you will punish someone more,
blocks.zh_text: 你也会更多地惩罚某个人，

blocks.en_text: you will blame someone more if I just said, "He broke it,"
blocks.zh_text: 如果我刚才说的是“他打碎了它”，你会更多地责怪某个人，

blocks.en_text: as opposed to, "It broke."
blocks.zh_text: 而不是说“它碎了”。

blocks.en_text: The language guides our reasoning about events.
blocks.zh_text: 语言引导着我们对事件的推理。

blocks.en_text: Now, I've given you a few examples
blocks.zh_text: 好了，我已经给你们举了几个例子，

blocks.en_text: of how language can profoundly shape the way we think,
blocks.zh_text: 说明语言如何能深刻地塑造我们的思维方式，

blocks.en_text: and it does so in a variety of ways.
blocks.zh_text: 而且它是以各种不同的方式做到这一点的。

blocks.en_text: So language can have big effects,
blocks.zh_text: 所以语言能产生很大的影响，

blocks.en_text: like we saw with space and time,
blocks.zh_text: 就像我们在空间和时间上看到的那样，

blocks.en_text: where people can lay out space and time
blocks.zh_text: 人们可以用完全不同的坐标框架

blocks.en_text: in completely different coordinate frames from each other.
blocks.zh_text: 来铺展空间和时间。

blocks.en_text: Language can also have really deep effects --
blocks.zh_text: 语言也能产生非常深远的影响——

blocks.en_text: that's what we saw with the case of number.
blocks.zh_text: 这就是我们在数字这个例子里看到的。

blocks.en_text: Having count words in your language,
blocks.zh_text: 你的语言里有计数词，

blocks.en_text: having number words,
blocks.zh_text: 有数字词，

blocks.en_text: opens up the whole world of mathematics.
blocks.zh_text: 就打开了整个数学世界的大门。

blocks.en_text: Of course, if you don't count, you can't do algebra,
blocks.zh_text: 当然，如果你不会数数，你就做不了代数，

blocks.en_text: you can't do any of the things
blocks.zh_text: 你也就做不了任何

blocks.en_text: that would be required to build a room like this
blocks.zh_text: 建造这样一个房间所必需的事情，

blocks.en_text: or make this broadcast, right?
blocks.zh_text: 或者做这场直播，对吧？

blocks.en_text: This little trick of number words gives you a stepping stone
blocks.zh_text: 数字词这个小把戏给了你一块垫脚石，

blocks.en_text: into a whole cognitive realm.
blocks.zh_text: 让你进入一个全新的认知领域。

blocks.en_text: Language can also have really early effects,
blocks.zh_text: 语言也能产生非常早期的影响，

blocks.en_text: what we saw in the case of color.
blocks.zh_text: 这就是我们在颜色这个例子里看到的。

blocks.en_text: These are really simple, basic, perceptual decisions.
blocks.zh_text: 这些都是非常简单的、基本的知觉判断。

blocks.en_text: We make thousands of them all the time,
blocks.zh_text: 我们每时每刻都在做成千上万个这样的判断，

blocks.en_text: and yet, language is getting in there
blocks.zh_text: 然而，语言却会介入其中，

blocks.en_text: and fussing even with these tiny little perceptual decisions that we make.
blocks.zh_text: 甚至对我们做出的这些微小的知觉判断也要插上一手。

blocks.en_text: Language can have really broad effects.
blocks.zh_text: 语言能产生非常广泛的影响。

blocks.en_text: So the case of grammatical gender may be a little silly,
blocks.zh_text: 所以语法性别这个例子可能有点好笑，

blocks.en_text: but at the same time, grammatical gender applies to all nouns.
blocks.zh_text: 但与此同时，语法性别适用于所有名词。

blocks.en_text: That means language can shape how you're thinking
blocks.zh_text: 这意味着语言能塑造你思考的方式，

blocks.en_text: about anything that can be named by a noun.
blocks.zh_text: 影响你对任何可以用名词来命名的事物的看法。

blocks.en_text: That's a lot of stuff.
blocks.zh_text: 那可是很多东西。

blocks.en_text: And finally, I gave you an example of how language can shape things
blocks.zh_text: 最后，我给你们举了一个例子，说明语言如何塑造

blocks.en_text: that have personal weight to us --
blocks.zh_text: 对我们个人有分量的事物——

blocks.en_text: ideas like blame and punishment or eyewitness memory.
blocks.zh_text: 比如责备和惩罚，或者目击者记忆这样的观念。

blocks.en_text: These are important things in our daily lives.
blocks.zh_text: 这些都是我们日常生活中重要的事情。

blocks.en_text: Now, the beauty of linguistic diversity is that it reveals to us
blocks.zh_text: 语言多样性的美妙之处在于，它向我们揭示了

blocks.en_text: just how ingenious and how flexible the human mind is.
blocks.zh_text: 人类心智是多么巧妙、多么灵活。

blocks.en_text: Human minds have invented not one cognitive universe, but 7,000 --
blocks.zh_text: 人类心智不只发明了一个认知宇宙，而是七千个——

blocks.en_text: there are 7,000 languages spoken around the world.
blocks.zh_text: 全世界有七千种语言在被使用。

blocks.en_text: And we can create many more --
blocks.zh_text: 而且我们还能创造更多——

blocks.en_text: languages, of course, are living things,
blocks.zh_text: 语言当然是活的东西，

blocks.en_text: things that we can hone and change to suit our needs.
blocks.zh_text: 是我们可以打磨、改变以适合自身需要的东西。

blocks.en_text: The tragic thing is that we're losing so much of this linguistic diversity
blocks.zh_text: 可悲的是，我们正在不断失去这么多语言多样性，

blocks.en_text: all the time.
blocks.zh_text: 一直在失去。

blocks.en_text: We're losing about one language a week,
blocks.zh_text: 我们大约每周失去一种语言，

blocks.en_text: and by some estimates,
blocks.zh_text: 而根据一些估计，

blocks.en_text: half of the world's languages will be gone in the next hundred years.
blocks.zh_text: 世界上半数语言将在未来一百年内消失。

blocks.en_text: And the even worse news is that right now,
blocks.zh_text: 更糟的消息是，现在，

blocks.en_text: almost everything we know about the human mind and human brain
blocks.zh_text: 我们所知道的关于人类心智和人类大脑的几乎一切，

blocks.en_text: is based on studies of usually American English-speaking undergraduates
blocks.zh_text: 都基于对通常说美式英语的本科生

blocks.en_text: at universities.
blocks.zh_text: 在大学里的研究。

blocks.en_text: That excludes almost all humans. Right?
blocks.zh_text: 这就几乎排除了全人类。对吧？

blocks.en_text: So what we know about the human mind is actually incredibly narrow and biased,
blocks.zh_text: 所以，我们对人类心智的了解其实非常狭窄，而且带有偏见，

blocks.en_text: and our science has to do better.
blocks.zh_text: 我们的科学必须做得更好。

blocks.en_text: I want to leave you with this final thought.
blocks.zh_text: 我想用最后一个想法来结束今天的演讲。

blocks.en_text: I've told you about how speakers of different languages think differently,
blocks.zh_text: 我跟你们讲了讲不同语言的使用者思维方式有多么不同，

blocks.en_text: but of course, that's not about how people elsewhere think.
blocks.zh_text: 但当然，这并不是说其他地方的人是怎么想的。

blocks.en_text: It's about how you think.
blocks.zh_text: 这说的是你自己是怎么想的。

blocks.en_text: It's how the language that you speak shapes the way that you think.
blocks.zh_text: 是你所说的语言塑造了你思考的方式。

blocks.en_text: And that gives you the opportunity to ask,
blocks.zh_text: 这就给了你一个机会去问：

blocks.en_text: "Why do I think the way that I do?"
blocks.zh_text: “我为什么会这样思考？”

blocks.en_text: "How could I think differently?"
blocks.zh_text: “我怎样才能换一种方式思考？”

blocks.en_text: And also,
blocks.zh_text: 还有，

blocks.en_text: "What thoughts do I wish to create?"
blocks.zh_text: “我希望创造出什么样的想法？”

blocks.en_text: Thank you very much.
blocks.zh_text: 非常感谢。
